mappings.note: Bare definition of wavelength, one of the four characteristics LO-6 lists. No LO-5 here, unlike O27, because the definition given is crest-to-crest rather than compression-to-compression.
SI unit of frequency. LO-6 again; nothing else in the frame names frequency.
Writes v = f-lambda. Recall of the relation, so LO-6 alone - LO-79 is reserved for items that actually produce a number.
Loudness as perceived amplitude: LO-73 for the perception, LO-6 for amplitude.
Timbre. Competency C2.7's text ('differences in what we hear as it propagates through different instruments') is the only place in the frame that describes sound quality; no learning outcome does.
Temperature and the speed of sound in one medium, so LO-6's speed rather than LO-3's comparison between states of matter.
The 0.1 s echo condition, which no outcome states. Cited at goal level; recorded as a gap.
Cause of reverberation - multiple reflections. Reflection has no outcome, and no building is being designed, so LO-75 is not claimed here.
Sound-absorbing panels in a concert hall: an architectural application of reflection, which is the nearest thing LO-75 covers. CG2 for the reflection physics.
Audible range stated as a frequency band: LO-6 for frequency, CG2 because human hearing limits appear nowhere as an outcome.
Names an animal that echolocates. Pure recall of an application with no mechanism to analyse, so unlike O56 no LO-77; CG2 alone.
SONAR expansion and purpose. No outcome mentions SONAR; recorded as a poor fit.
One medical application of ultrasound. Same gap as the other ultrasound items; nothing in the frame reaches medical technology.
Below 20 Hz is a frequency classification (LO-6) into the infrasonic band, which only CG2 can carry.
Binaural hearing. The frame has no ear or hearing outcome at all, so a single goal-level code; recorded as a poor fit.

The one item in the chapter that LO-76 ('Display awareness about Sir C.V. Raman') fits exactly, with its goal CG6 and the India competency C6.1. Not LO-74, whose text is about music rather than about a scientist.
Sonic boom from supersonic flight. No outcome covers it, so CG2, with LO-77 because the item asks what RESULTS from a described real-life situation.
Explains the larynx mechanism: LO-1 for the vibrating part and LO-2 for the causal step from vibration to sound, both of which the three-mark answer must contain.
Describe the experiment AND state the property: C8.2 for the procedure, LO-4 for the conclusion it supports.
Propagation by compressions and rarefactions - LO-5 in full. Nothing is drawn or computed, so no process code.
Draw and label the density-distance graph (LO-78) marking crest, trough, wavelength and amplitude (LO-6). The drawing requirement is what distinguishes it from S92.
Derives v = f-lambda from the definitions of speed, wavelength and time period - three items from LO-6's own list. A derivation, not a numeric prediction, so no LO-79.
Loudness is LO-73's; INTENSITY as energy per unit area per unit time is a physical quantity the frame never names, so CG2 carries that half. The contrast between the two is the whole question.
Reverberation plus its architectural remedy, so LO-75 for the built acoustic space alongside CG2.
SONAR principle and application, explained but not computed. CG2 alone; adding LO-79 would be wrong since no result is predicted.
